Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Summary assessment: Chronic palm-dominant dermatitis with severe dryness, cracking, and pruritus in a hotel housekeeper with intermittent glove use and exposure to cleaning products; lifestyle and occupational exposures likely contributing; diabetes present as a metabolic comorbidity with broader skin dryness risk.
- Relevant DDx considerations incorporated:
  - Irritant contact dermatitis (High likelihood): Occupational exposure to cleaning agents; inconsistent glove use; palm-dominant involvement; chronicity.
  - Allergic contact dermatitis (Moderate-High likelihood): Possible sensitization to cleaning agents; pruritus and fissuring compatible; patch testing consideration.
  - Hand dermatitis/eczema including possible atopic component (Medium likelihood): Chronic dry, itchy hands; may be exacerbated by irritants or allergens; response to steroids and emollients typical.
  - Xerosis due to diabetes/metabolic factors (Low likelihood): Diabetes can cause dry skin, but focal palmar cracking with itching favors dermatitis over simple xerosis.
- Conflicts: None identified between transcript and DDx. Conflict noted if any were present. Not recorded.

Management Plan
- Management plan main: 
  - Wear gloves during cleaning at all times; minimize exposure to irritants
  - Start topical corticosteroid to affected palms for inflammation
  - Apply stronger emollients/coats three to four times daily for the next 2 weeks
  - Follow-up in 1–2 weeks or sooner if spreading or worsening
  - Prescription to pharmacy provided for medications

- Hand dermatitis/eczema (including possible atopic component) — Medium
